title: I can't code a deckbuilder. Claude Code and my own asset packs did it anyway: 10 heroes, 99 enemies, 156 cards
author: _AssetSmithy_
selftext:
I make and sell 2D game assets on itch (backgrounds, battlers, card frames, icons, UI). This time I wanted to build a full game out of them, so I did.  
  
This is Clanbound, a roguelike deckbuilder in the vein of Monster Train and Wildfrost. You summon creatures onto a battle line, play spells and attacks, and fight your way through 3 acts to the final boss.  
  
What's in it:  
\- 10 heroes, each with their own deck and starting relic  
\- 156 cards (67 of them creatures) across 7 clans  
\- 99 enemies, including 27 elites and 11 bosses  
\- 44 relics, 12 potions, card upgrades  
\- 28 events with voiced NPCs who react to your choices, 132 spoken lines  
\- A branching map of 15 floors per act, with merchant, campfire, treasure, save and continue  
  
How I made it:  
The art and music come from my own asset packs, created with AI tools and cleaned up by me. The NPC voices and sound effects were generated separately with ElevenLabs. Every line of code was written by Claude Code. I set the direction, played every build and gave feedback, from "the shadow is in the wrong place" to "make the campfire look more real". Even the effects like the fire, the heat shimmer and the depth of field in the backgrounds are shaders Claude wrote.  
  
The version you can play is a second build. The first one was Unity WebGL and took close to a minute to load, which kills a browser game. So Claude ported the whole thing to plain HTML5 and PixiJS, no engine, 1:1 including the shaders and the particle effects. We ran both builds side by side on the same seeds and the combat came out identical. Now it is playable a few seconds after you open the page.  
  
It's free and runs right in your browser. Balancing is still done by feel, so any feedback is welcome: what's too easy, too hard, what's missing?  
  
**You can play it here:** [https://assetsmithy.itch.io/clanbound](https://assetsmithy.itch.io/clanbound)

comments.author: Ziadjbt78
comments.body: Love the gameplay and animation, truly impressive. How long it took you to code with Claude? I’m sure despite AI involvement this takes quite a long time and loads of effort to put together am I right? Whats your plans for the future? Expansions, improvements, etc?

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
Thanks, that means a lot!  
  
The browser version took about six hours of hands-on time over two evenings. The build in the video took longer, and on top of that come the asset packs themselves, which took months.   
  
So yes, you are right. The AI writes the code fast, but it does not know what is fun, what is unreadable on screen or what feels off in the third fight. That part is still me, and that is where the time goes. I play, note things like "the map wastes half the parchment", and it gets fixed in minutes instead of hours. The speed is real, the direction is not free.  
  
Plans: balancing first, since it is still done by feel, then more events and cards. It stays free, it is a showcase for my asset packs, so no paid expansions. Tell me what felt too easy or too hard and that is what the next pass is built on.
